clue.text: Crazy speculator opening mine with sign of trouble on plant

parts.note: cuckoo is slang for mad or crazy

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from speculator

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A mad speculator starts digging a mine and finds a warning sign on some plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes the first letter of 'speculator'. 'Opening mine' reads as starting a mine, but the two words do different jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The frothy blobs left by froghopper larvae on garden stems are a familiar sign of insect trouble.

clue.text: One there with a letter, say about ten old pence

indicators.note: about means going round, so the letter's name surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T
taken as written
d was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Someone present carries a letter, perhaps costing around tenpence in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the spelt-out letter round the rest. Before 1971 British pennies were written d, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends an event is a person who is there, present at it.

clue.text: Bear heavy makeweight?

parts.note: padding is material added just to make up bulk, like a makeweight
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A question about whether a bear is a hefty bit of filler.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in the reverse of the clue's order: a heavy makeweight is padding weighing a ton. Paddington is the bear from the children's books, named after a London railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru found at a London station.

clue.text: Boy asking for money

definitions.meaning: A common boy's name, short for William

explanation.definitionFit: Bill is a short form of the boy's name William, and an invoice asks you to pay.

clue.text: Chaucer's verse, a holy and merry blend

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so these letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chaucer's poetry is described as a mixture of the pious and the jolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blend' rearranges A HOLY and MERRY; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme royal is the seven-line stanza Chaucer used in Troilus and Criseyde, so it is his verse form.

clue.text: See 1
Harm in disclosing how old mother is?

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
age is the answer to how old something is

explanation.surface: Is it hurtful to reveal your mother's age?
explanation.walkthrough: Telling how old mother is gives the dam's age. Dam is a breeder's word for a female parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is a synonym for harm, injury done to something.

clue.text: County for a few: rest will be different

parts.note: some means a small number, a few

indicators.note: the word rest is to become different, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A county suits a few people, while the rest will feel otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be different' rearranges REST to RSET. Somerset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is one of the counties of south-west England.

clue.text: Frequency with which Hugh gets involved with trial

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so these letters are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of how often a man called Hugh gets drawn into a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved' mixes HUGH with TRIAL; the final 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultrahigh frequency (UHF) is a radio band, so the word describes a kind of frequency.

clue.text: Theatrical item for audience to philosopher

indicators.note: for an audience means as heard, so a word's sound is used

parts.note: a play is an item of theatre
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stage production is put on in honour of an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for audience' says PLAY is heard, not spelt: PLAY followed by TO sounds like the name, which is said PLAY-toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: Dumpling for soup and joint on plate I had put in

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across clue, so the joint comes first
put in signals that the next piece is inserted into the others

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
I had contracts to I'd
an L-plate is the plate shown by a learner driver, giving L

explanation.surface: A dumpling recipe calls for a joint sitting on a plate with something added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places the contraction inside joint-on-plate, after its third letter. A kneidel is a matzo-ball dumpling served in Jewish chicken soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A kneidel is a matzo-meal dumpling traditionally served floating in chicken soup.

clue.text: Macbeth stating his rank could be fiery

parts.note: Macbeth speaking of himself would say me
Macbeth held the rank of thane, a Scottish lord

explanation.surface: Macbeth, announcing his title, might turn out to be hot-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth is Thane of Glamis and then Cawdor in Shakespeare's play, so he might announce himself as 'me, thane'.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a highly flammable gas, the firedamp that explodes in mines, so it can burst into flame.

clue.text: Source of cronyism for crooked lord and king, including battle flower for two

indicators.note: including means containing, so the first pieces wrap round the rest
crooked means bent out of shape, so this word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the Boyne is both a 1690 battle and an Irish river, a flower being something that flows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone corrupt explains cronyism through a bent lord, a king, a battle and a bloom for a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the lord to OLDR, and 'including' sets the battle and the number inside that plus K, after its third letter. In crosswords a flower is often a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The network of former pupils of elite schools helping one another is a classic source of cronyism.

clue.text: Crazy fellow, crazy for shelling

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person
crackers is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A madman, utterly mad, gets ready for a bombardment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shelling' suggests gunfire, but it means removing shells from nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcrackers are the hinged tool used to crack open nuts, so they are a device used for removing shells.

clue.text: Three-wheeler's about turn, ideally, when people are out but not down

definitions.text: when people are out but not down

indicators.note: about means around, so the trike surrounds the following pieces

parts.note: a trike is a three-wheeled cycle
a U-turn gives U for turn
best means in the ideal way

explanation.surface: A three-wheeled vehicle making an about turn is ideal when workers are out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the turn and 'ideally' inside the vehicle; the 's is just 'has'. In a stoppage on the London Underground (the Tube) workers are out, and no one goes down to the trains.
explanation.definitionFit: During a stoppage on the London Underground, staff walk out and passengers cannot go down to the platforms.

clue.text: Setting for tribunal giving old solver the runaround?

indicators.note: around signals the run is placed around the next piece

parts.note: a course is a run, a route taken
thou is the old form of you, the solver being addressed

explanation.surface: A court building gives an elderly puzzler the runaround.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaround' splits into run and around, so the old form of you sits inside the run. Setters often address the solver as you.
explanation.definitionFit: A courthouse is the building where courts and tribunals sit, so it is the setting for hearings.

clue.text: Female cosmonaut in paper?

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
ET, the extraterrestrial, is used loosely for a space traveller

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a woman in space.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet is a single piece of paper.

clue.text: Damage caused by a larva in a herb

indicators.note: in signals the larva goes inside the herb

parts.note: sage is a culinary herb
a bot is the larva of the botfly

explanation.surface: Plants are ruined by a grub living in a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the article and the grub inside the herb; the botfly's larva is called a bot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is deliberate destruction or damage done to wreck something.

clue.text: See 13
A place to sleep in Paris without illumination

parts.note: un is French for a, the 'in Paris' covering this word too
lit is French for bed

explanation.surface: A Parisian bed for the night has no lights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' asks for French words: UN for 'a' and LIT for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlit has no light shining on it, so it is lacking illumination.

clue.text: Extended millrace in safari park

parts.note: long means extended in length
a leat is an open channel bringing water to a mill

explanation.surface: A long mill stream runs through a wildlife park.
explanation.walkthrough: Longleat is a stately home in Wiltshire, England, famous for its drive-through safari park.
explanation.definitionFit: Longleat in Wiltshire was the first drive-through safari park outside Africa.

clue.text: Crazy student in mine is sweet

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy

indicators.note: in signals the student goes inside the mine

parts.note: a pit is a mine
L is for learner, a student

explanation.surface: A mad student down a mine is a lovely person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside PIT. 'Sweet' looks like a description of the student, but it is the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana split is a dessert, and a dessert is a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: African flower produced by gardener in England

indicators.note: the flower is produced by, made from, the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An African bloom has been grown by an English gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' points to letters running through gardeNER IN England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerine is a genus of South African bulbs with bright lily-like flowers.

clue.text: See 13
Doing one's best to be vexatious?

definitions.meaning: making an attempt, giving something a go

explanation.definitionFit: Attempting hard is making an effort, and a tiresome thing is irritating and hard to endure.

clue.text: Demarcation dispute between racehorse trainers?

parts.note: a fight over territory, imagined as a battle on the racecourse, where the grass track is the turf

explanation.definitionFit: A fight between rival groups over who controls an area is a dispute over boundaries.

clue.text: See 13
Mobile carrier — one's crazy to be off it

definitions.meaning: a wheeled cart for carrying things

definitions.text: one's crazy to be off it

explanation.definitionFit: A wheeled cart is a mobile carrier, and 'off one's trolley' is British slang for mad.

clue.text: Caterpillar container

definitions.meaning: a tracked armoured vehicle, running on caterpillar tracks
a vessel for holding liquid or gas

explanation.definitionFit: An armoured fighting vehicle runs on caterpillar tracks, and a large vessel holds water or fuel.

clue.text: Good one at end of year is finished

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here from year

explanation.surface: A good person arriving at the end of the year is done for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes the last letter of 'year'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something doomed beyond saving is described as done for, all over.

clue.text: Chessman with family — young produced on a string

indicators.note: on means placed after in an across clue, so the young follow the string

parts.note: kin are one's family
G is one of the strings of a violin or guitar
spawn is the young produced by fish or frogs

explanation.surface: A chess piece and its relatives, with offspring dangling on a string.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the young come after the string, not before it as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The king's pawn is the pawn standing in front of the king at the start of a chess game.
